purpose: Exploratory reanalysis of an existing public cohort to measure the canonical and +29-nt UBASH3A junctions directly. This is not a novel cohort or a held-out AlphaGenome benchmark.
recorded_before: Retrieval or inspection of Snaptron target-junction counts and GEUVADIS rs1893592 genotype groups in this follow-up
prior_selection: Targets selected from the earlier AlphaGenome prediction, literature and Lepik summary-statistic result. GEUVADIS was previously used in Ji et al. 2017.
data_source: Snaptron srav3h / recount3 public RNA-seq junction counts; GEUVADIS ERP001942 sample metadata; public 1000 Genomes genotypes
sample_rules: Restrict RNA-seq libraries to verified ERP001942 study membership.
Match public pseudonymous donor IDs to public genotypes explicitly; exclude ambiguous or missing mappings.
Aggregate technical libraries by donor before any inference; libraries are not independent biological samples.
Do not infer genotypes from the RNA endpoint itself.
Primary descriptive cohort uses European populations CEU, FIN, GBR and TSI; report other populations separately if available.
Require canonical plus plus29 junction read count >=10 per donor for the primary ratio. Report retention and genotype-group sizes. A prespecified >=20 sensitivity check may be reported separately.
Keep zero plus29 counts when canonical coverage is sufficient. A missing query or unverified sample coverage must not be converted into zero.
endpoint: plus29 / (canonical + plus29) junction-supporting read ratio. This is a two-junction composition, not the fraction of all UBASH3A transcripts or a full intron-retention measurement.
analysis: Report per-genotype donor counts and distributions of both junction counts and the ratio.
If metadata and sample coverage support inference, estimate the ratio change per C allele with population fixed effects and heteroskedasticity-robust uncertainty, using donors as units.
Keep all outcomes including disagreements, sparse coverage, failed access and insufficient metadata.
No disease-risk, protein-effect, therapeutic or causal inference from this comparison. No new AlphaGenome calls are needed.
